review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read its two downstream users, CurvePlaceSectionDivisor.lean and CurvePlaceSectionOrder.lean, and grepped the repo for uses of the file's lemmas. The only simp lemma here is `divisor_apply`. It is `rfl` and has the right orientation, because it unfolds the `Finsupp` coercion of `divisor` into `orderAt`. `orderAt` is a def that is not simp-unfolded, so there is no unwanted expansion. The right-hand side cannot loop back to `divisor`. The sibling `CurvePlaceSectionDivisor.divisor_apply` is about a different `divisor` and a different head symbol, so the two do not compete. Its right-hand side is `orderAt ...`, which this file's `divisor_apply` does not rewrite. The other lemmas are `mem_zero_support_iff_not_isUnit` and `orderAt_eq_zero_of_not_mem`. They are conditional or typeclass-heavy, and the repo only calls them explicitly in proofs. I found no use that would justify a simp attribute. I did not see any case where the simp set pattern-matches wrongly, and I could not run Lean, so I made no claims about observed simp behaviour.
